content.text:
SCIM `POST /Users` now always creates the user in local storage, so a federation provider can no longer take the new user. I haven't compiled or tested the change. A standalone offline `mvn compile -pl scim/model` failed because `keycloak-scim-core` and `keycloak-model-jpa` 999.0.0-SNAPSHOT aren't in the local Maven repo.

The change is in `UserResourceTypeProvider.onCreate` (`scim/model`). It used to call `UserProfile.create(false)`, which goes through `session.users().addUser()`. That call hands the user to the first enabled `UserRegistrationProvider`, such as LDAP in import mode, which is why a successful POST could return an ID that a SCIM GET couldn't find. It now calls `UserStoragePrivateUtil.userLocalStorage(session).addUser(realm, username.toLowerCase())`. That is the same local storage the SCIM read paths query, and the lowercasing matches what the normal local-creation path does.

`populate()` and `persist()` still run afterwards through the SCIM user profile, so validation and attribute handling are the same as before. The edit also removes the `UserProfileProvider` local that `onCreate` no longer uses; every import in the file is still used.

I didn't implement the optional ideas from the issue, such as per-provider capability checks or a configurable federation strategy.
